name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  November 7, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the
City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:02 p.m.,
on November 7, 2011, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on November 2, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  W. Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Reardon

INVOCATION: Mayor Leckness

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations — The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator

City Council Minutes  1  November 7, 2011
   Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City's Unrepresented Employee (Assistant City
  Manager.) The City's Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Mayor Pro Tem Ury
was absent.)

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council provided direction to staff but there was no
reportable action from Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Administer Attorney Oath to Resident Thomas Colby

  Mayor Leckness administered the attorney’s oath to Thomas Colby.

P2.  Capo Valley High School Girls Tennis Team Recognition

  Mayor Leckness presented Certificates of Commendation to the coaches and members of
  the Capistrano Valley High School Girls Varsity Tennis Team.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Maurer, M.V.: speaking on behalf of the Friends of the Mission Viejo Library, he outlined
the services the library provides to residents of the community.

Bob Hayes, M.V.: discussed the importance of our country’s national holidays and he noted that
the reason we observe Veterans Day, formerly Armistice Day, is to commemorate the end of
World War I.

Steve Magdziak, M.V.: asked why the Assistant City Manager’s contract is being discussed in a
closed door meeting and he requested that the matter be considered in open session.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: thanked the Mayor and staff for a great campout event. He also
expressed concern that the Orange County Fire Authority is not bidding a broker-dealer contract.

City Council Minutes  2  November 7, 2011
 Beverly Ann Killingback, M.V.: stated that she is handicapped and she needs to keep a 23-foot
vehicle in her driveway because it helps her with the care and independence that she needs.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 6, 7, and 10 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Ury

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of October 17, 2011, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register dated October 7, 2011 in the amount of $2,144,814.53

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated October 14, 2011 in the amount of $734,681.44

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated October 21, 2011 in the amount of $996,642.11

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

8.  Approval of CalPERS Requirement for a Publicly Available Pay Schedule

City Council Minutes  3  November 7, 2011
   Adopted Resolution 11-68 Amending the City's Salary Schedule and Establishing Salary
  Ranges for Authorized Job Classifications.

9.  Orange  County  Transportation  Authority  2011-2012  Comprehensive
  Transportation Funding Program Call-for-Projects.

  (1) Adopted Resolution 11-69 Approving the Submittal of Candidate City of Mission
  Viejo Transportation Projects to the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)
  for Funding Consideration Under the OCTA Comprehensive Transportation Funding
  Program for Regional Capacity Projects; (2) adopted Resolution 11-70 Approving the
  Submittal of the Oso Parkway Corridor, the Santa Margarita Parkway Corridor, and the
  Los Alisos Boulevard Corridor Improvement Projects to the Orange County
  Transportation Authority for Funding Under the Competitive Measure M2 Regional
  Transportation Signal Synchronization Program; and (3) directed staff to transmit both
  resolutions to OCTA by December 2, 2011, in conjunction with the City’s funding
  applications for said projects.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

11.  Public Hearing to Consider All Objections to the Proposed Abatement of Weeds on
  Parcels Less than One Acre for the Annual Weed Abatement Program - Year 2011 -
  Phase 2 - Round II

  At the hour of 6:40 p.m., Mayor Leckness opened the public hearing. Upon hearing no
  requests to speak, Mayor Leckness closed the public hearing.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Rattay presented the staff report.

  The City Council Members inquired about the number of homes that are on the list for
  weed abatement, under what circumstances the homes ended up on the list, and what the
  homeowners will be charged to remove the weeds.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  instruct the Public Services Department to proceed and perform the removal of weeds in
  accordance with Sections 39568 through 39588 of the Government Code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

City Council Minutes  4  November 7, 2011
 OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

6.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - First Quarter of 2011-12

  Council Member Reardon asked questions regarding revenue figures, reserves, CEFV
  funds and depreciation, and whether or not the city is in a deficit at the present time.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas noted that revenues do not come in
  evenly throughout the year. Staff believes that the city is on track with its
  revenue estimations as they know the money is going to come in. Ms. Dyas said she
  believes that the City will end the fiscal year in a positive situation. She further described
  the City’s replacement funds, depreciation, and equipment replacement practices. She
  also discussed the notion of deficit spending and the timing of capital project spending.

  Council Member Kelley noted that the City has been very accurate in hitting its revenue
  and expenditure projections. In the agenda report, the general fund discretionary reserves
  are listed at $25.5 million and 53% of the general fund group revenues. She stated that
  the City has done a good job of holding its reserves above the 40-50% target.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with the City’s forecasting practices and she
  stated that we are not paying attention to operating costs and revenues are not keeping
  pace.

  City Manager Wilberg responded that the City has cut its operating costs over the last
  several years and the entire Council was made aware of that.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

7.  Quarterly Financial Report for the Community Development Agency - First
  Quarter of 2011-12

City Council Minutes  5  November 7, 2011
   Council Member Schlicht stated that she doesn’t understand how the City can earmark
  $10 million for developers, with no contract to back it up, when the CDA has been
  suspended.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to receive and
  file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

10.  Purchase of Replacement Computer Systems

  Jackie Alexander, Director of Information Technology, presented the staff report. She
  noted that IT staff supports 284 users on the City’s network. There are 180 computers
  assigned to these individuals which means that many share a computer. Additionally 52
  computers will be installed in the library for public use and 18 will be placed in a loan
  program.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  authorize staff to issue a purchase order to Dell, Inc. for an amount not to exceed
  $295,000 for purchase of replacement computer systems.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

12.  Community Services Commission Appointment

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  appoint Ron Ruef to the Community Services Commission, effective January 2012.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  6  November 7, 2011
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury

13.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the Orange County Fire Authority lacks credibility
  in his book and he stated that they continually violate the Public Records Act.

14.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Leckness announced that there was nothing to report from the Foothill/Eastern
  TCA in Mayor Pro Tem Ury’s absence.

15.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Leckness announced that he had nothing to report from the San Joaquin Hills
  TCA.

16.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg announced that the refinancing of the freeway center bonds will close on
November 8, saving the property owners about $350,000.

City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Curley discussed AB 32, the California Global Warming Solutions Act. He also
noted that he is working to craft a child safety zone ordinance and he asked the Council for
direction regarding the definition of a park.

By consensus, the City Council expressed a preference to use the wording “city owned or
maintained parks” in the ordinance.

City Council Minutes  7  November 7, 2011
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

17.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that she attended the Olympic finish line completion
ceremony on October 25 and she encouraged residents to visit the monument to see the
wonderful new additions such as the seating area and the water fountain. She noted that during
the ceremony, the City recognized prominent resident Ziggy Wilczynski and unveiled the Rotary
Club’s bear statue in his honor. Council Member Kelley thanked Mayor Leckness for his part in
preparing the special recognition for Mr. Wilczynski. She also commended staff and the
Saddleback Unified School District recreation department for another great Home Town
Halloween. She got to enjoy this year’s event through the eyes of her grandsons and she stated
that it is such a good program that the City offers to the community. Council Member Kelley
reminded residents of two Veterans Day ceremonies on November 11, one hosted by the City at
the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center at 2:00 p.m., and the other at El Toro
Memorial Cemetery at 11:00 a.m. Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of
Character word for the month of November is thankfulness.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon echoed Council Member Kelley’s sentiments about Hometown
Halloween and stated that she took three of her grandsons and they all had a wonderful time.
She also enjoyed the Walk Against Drugs with key note speaker Mark Munoz and she thanked
staff and Crime Prevention Specialist Tammy Descoteaux for doing a great job with that event
and with the Disaster Preparedness Expo. Council Member Reardon outlined her attendance at
additional events including the Freedom Awards Ceremony at the Sheriff’s training academy in
Tustin, the Olympic finish line completion ceremony, and her site visit to the Outta Bounds
program at the Potocki Center. She encouraged her colleagues to visit the center and become
fully acquainted with Outta Bounds before the Council is asked to decide on a future use for the
Potocki Center. Council Member Reardon discussed her attendance at the Orange County 2-1-1
update on the 10-year plan to end homelessness. She stated that homelessness is not what it has
been in the past as so many people have lost their jobs and their homes, as a result. Council
Member Reardon concluded her comments by sharing a video montage of young Cade Spinello
who is recovering from brain tumor surgery and a stroke.

City Council Minutes  8  November 7, 2011
 Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht discussed Veterans Day and the meaning of the upcoming holiday.
She announced that the City’s ceremony will be held on Friday, November 11, 2011, from 2:00
to 4:00 p.m. She encouraged residents to attend the City’s ceremony as well as the Elks Club
Veterans tribute on November 8, beginning at 6:00 p.m. Council Member Schlicht asked if staff
has reached out to former City Manager Dan Joseph who has recently written a book about his
father. She suggested that Mr. Joseph may want to do a book signing at the library. She also
discussed a letter that the Council received from a resident who asked to opt-out of the SCE
smart meter installation, yet she received a smart meter anyway. Council Member Schlicht
recommended that anyone with a similar problem should register a complaint with the CPUC.
She outlined her attendance at recent events including the Capistrano Valley High School
Foundation’s Taste of Capo Valley, the Walk Against Drugs and Disaster Preparedness Expo,
and the American Legion Pancake breakfast where she met a retired U.S. Navy war hero named
Commander Bill Hardy. She further discussed her invitation to be a guest at a Mission Viejo
High School Humanities Class. She noted that the students were terrific and well-informed and
it gave her a good feeling about our nation’s future. Council Member Schlicht announced that the
MVHS Diablos Mustang game is Thursday, not Friday, this week and she added that she
attended a recent Casta Del Sol’s Republican Club meeting where she was a guest speaker along
with Assemblyman Todd Spitzer. Council Member Schlicht concluded her comments by
expressing concern with the City’s finances. She noted that the City of Laguna Niguel saved up
for a new city hall and they completed it on time and under budget. She referred to Mission
Viejo’s report to the State Controller and she disagreed with the notion that Mission Viejo saves
up for its projects.

Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Mayor Leckness

Mayor Leckness expressed his appreciation to Keith Rattay for his work on the Ziggy the Bear
statue at the Olympic finish line. He also outlined his attendance at a ribbon cutting ceremony at
Rampage Jackson, a visit to Oxford Prep School where he observed the children learning the
National Anthem, and his attendance at the Walk Against Drugs and Disaster Preparedness expo.
Mayor Leckness thanked City staff for planning such a fantastic Campout with the Mayor, the
City’s first event of its kind, and he read a thank you note from residents who attended the
campout.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:36 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Leckness adjourned the meeting to Monday, November 21, 2011, at 5:00 p.m.

City Council Minutes  9  November 7, 2011
 __________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 21, 2011

City Council Minutes  10  November 7, 2011
